readings: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then average those patient-level figures for each sex. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round.
queries:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(l.ALB) AS avg_alb,
        AVG(l.UN * 1.0 / NULLIF(l."T-BIL", 0)) AS avg_un_tbil_ratio
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_averages AS (
    SELECT
        SEX,
        AVG(avg_alb) AS avg_alb,
        AVG(avg_un_tbil_ratio) AS avg_un_tbil_ratio
    FROM patient_averages
    GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT
    SEX,
    avg_alb,
    avg_un_tbil_ratio,
    avg_alb - (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) FROM sex_averages) AS alb_above_mean
FROM sex_averages
WHERE avg_alb > (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) FROM sex_averages)
